feature1.prompt: Migration crashes deleting an index_together if there is a unique_together on the same fields. This problem occurs with Django 1.11.10 where attempting to delete an index_together results in a ValueError because the deletion routine finds both an index and a unique constraint on the same fields. The fix must ensure that when deleting an index_together, only the index portion is removed and the unique_together constraint remains intact. Moreover, altering the declaration of an index should not trigger its re-creation unintentionally.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on modifying the core deletion logic in the schema handling. Update the call to _delete_composed_index in django/db/backends/base/schema.py so that it passes an extra parameter ('unique': False) along with 'index': True. This change should guarantee that only the index constraint is removed while any unique_together constraint remains unaffected.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/backends/base/schema.py; Function: alter_index_together. In the block that calls _delete_composed_index (around line 393 in the diff), update the dictionary argument to include 'unique': False.

feature2.prompt: Migration crashes deleting an index_together if there is a unique_together on the same fields. This issue arises when both an index and a unique constraint are declared on the same set of fields, leading to a ValueError that states 'Found wrong number (2) of constraints'. The resolution must ensure that during the deletion process only the index portion is removed, leaving the unique_together constraint intact. Furthermore, changes to the declaration of an index should not result in its unnecessary re-creation.
feature2.hint_texts: Enhance the test suite to validate that the unique_together constraint remains unaffected when an index_together is removed. Developers should add tests that first confirm the existence of the unique constraint and then verify that after an index deletion the unique constraint still exists. Update the test files by introducing a new assertion method and a complementary test case that simulates the problematic migration scenario.
feature2.entrypoint: Modify the following test files: In tests/migrations/test_base.py, add a new assertion method named 'assertUniqueConstraintExists'. In tests/migrations/test_operations.py, add a new test called 'test_alter_index_together_remove_with_unique_together' that first checks for the unique constraint, then applies the migration altering the index_together, and finally verifies that the unique constraint remains.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: The files django/db/backends/base/schema.py, tests/migrations/test_base.py, tests/migrations/test_operations.py, and the overall migration framework are shared between both features.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1's changes to the deletion logic must be validated by Feature2's enhanced test suite. Both teams should integrate their changes to ensure that the unique_together constraints remain preserved through index_together modifications and that the migration operations behave correctly.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers responsible for Feature1 and Feature2 should maintain regular communication to align their changes, ensuring the schema modifications and test enhancements work seamlessly together. Discussions should cover integration details, shared resource impacts, and validation strategies.
